"""One stub page per notable new entity (action=create), schema-routed.

    Unknown entity types (no schema at all) build no stub here and are left
    in proposal.entity_resolutions — validate_proposal() reports those as a
    hard stop, which is correct: the type is genuinely unrecognized.

    Types that DO have a schema but no canonical directory (e.g. `index`,
    a MOC/nav page with nowhere to be filed) are a different situation:
    the source is real and recognized, it just needs manual placement.
    A warning is recorded so the skip is visible in the enrich preview, and
    the resolution is dropped from proposal.entity_resolutions so
    validate_proposal's create-scanning loop never sees it — otherwise its
    hard stop would abort the entire apply (including this proposal's
    unrelated proposed_note and other stubs/updates) over a case that's
    already been surfaced as a warning, not an error.

    Extraction (proposed_note) and entity resolution are independent model
    calls, and both can independently decide to represent the *same*
    real-world subject — usually under a different entity type, so the
    proposed path never collides with proposed_note.path even though it's a
    duplicate in substance. A create-resolution whose slugified name matches
    proposed_note's own name/title is suppressed here rather than written as
    a second, always-empty page for the same subject (see issue #36).
    """
    schemas = load_entity_schemas(config.root_path)
    today = datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()
    stubs: list[ProposedFile] = []
    taken = {proposal.proposed_note.path} if proposal.proposed_note else set()
    kept_resolutions: list[EntityResolution] = []
    proposed_note_slug = _proposed_note_subject_slug(proposal.proposed_note)

    for resolution in proposal.entity_resolutions:
        if resolution.action != "create":
            kept_resolutions.append(resolution)
            continue
        schema = schemas.get(resolution.entity_type)
        if schema is None:
            # Genuinely unknown type: keep it in entity_resolutions so
            # validate_proposal's hard stop still fires for it.
            proposal.warnings.append(
                f"{resolution.name}: type '{resolution.entity_type}' has no canonical "
                "directory to route into — needs manual placement"
            )
            kept_resolutions.append(resolution)
            continue
        if schema.directory is None:
            # Known type, no canonical directory: warn and drop, so
            # validate_proposal doesn't hard-stop the whole apply over it.
            proposal.warnings.append(
                f"{resolution.name}: type '{resolution.entity_type}' has no canonical "
                "directory to route into — needs manual placement"
            )
            continue
        resolution_slug = slugify(resolution.name)
        if proposed_note_slug is not None and resolution_slug == proposed_note_slug:
            proposal.warnings.append(
                f"{resolution.name}: already represented by the proposed note "
                f"({proposal.proposed_note.path}) — not creating a duplicate page"
            )
            kept_resolutions.append(resolution)
            continue
        path = f"{schema.directory}/{slugify(resolution.name)}.md"

"""One-off: give the 6 status-less ISSUES.jsonl entries a real status, and
close out the stale #39 feedback comments on ids 20-23 with a fresh 'open'
one noting the create-path confidence gap PR #52 didn't cover."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

path = Path.home() / "Projects" / "kb-personal" / "ISSUES.jsonl"
TODAY = "2026-07-27"

# Genuinely unaddressed by any of the 11 merged PRs -- no code path touches
# their root cause (dropped-content-empty-stub on a fresh single-source
# create, timeline-placeholder date, frontmatter quoting, "untitled"

OPEN_UNFIXED = {4, 10, 47, 51, 94}

# #36's merged fix (suppress a create-resolution stub whose subject matches
# proposed_note's own name/title) is directly relevant to the type: source
# stray-duplicate risk this entry describes -- worth a fresh look now that
# it's merged, even though no issue was filed for this id specifically.
READY_NOW = {3}

# #39/PR #52 only added EntityRevision.confidence (the update path). All
# four of these are fresh action=create book entities, never revisited by
# an update in this migration -- the create-path gap (EntityResolution.
# proposed_frontmatter carries no confidence) is untouched.
CONFIDENCE_CREATE_PATH_GAP_IDS = {20, 21, 22, 23}
NEW_COMMENT_TEXT = (
    "wakil PR #52 (merged into main) added a `confidence` field to "
    "`EntityRevision`, but scoped to the UPDATE path only (frontmatter_updates "
    "on an existing page) -- confirmed by reading the merged ingest_service.py "
    "and the PR's own description, which explicitly left EntityResolution."
    "proposed_frontmatter (the CREATE path, used by _build_stub_entities for a "
    "brand-new entity like this one) untouched. This entry's status: field was "
    "inferred at entity-creation time, not via a later update, so the merged "
    "fix does not apply here -- the underlying gap (no confidence signal on a "
    "freshly-created entity's inferred frontmatter) remains open."
)

lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
out = []
touched = []
for line in lines:
    if not line.strip():
        out.append(line)
        continue
    obj = json.loads(line)
    oid = obj["id"]

    if oid in OPEN_UNFIXED:
        obj["status"] = "open"
        touched.append((oid, "status->open"))
    elif oid in READY_NOW:
        obj["status"] = "ready to be confirmed"
        touched.append((oid, "status->ready to be confirmed"))

    if oid in CONFIDENCE_CREATE_PATH_GAP_IDS:
        for comment in obj.get("feedback", []):
            comment["status"] = "closed"
        obj.setdefault("feedback", []).append(
            {"comment date": TODAY, "comment": NEW_COMMENT_TEXT, "status": "open"}
        )
        touched.append((oid, "feedback closed+reopened"))

    out.append(json.dumps(obj))

path.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")
for oid, action in touched:
    print(f"id={oid}: {action}")

# wakil fixes — 2026-07-27 — confirming-agent brief

Handoff for the agent re-testing `ISSUES.jsonl` entries against the current
wakil install. Read this before re-running confirmation passes — it explains
what changed underneath you since the last pass, and which entries are
genuinely worth re-testing vs. already settled.

## What changed

11 GitHub issues (`ebridges/wakil` #36–#46) were filed from the first 114
`ISSUES.jsonl` entries, each root-caused against wakil's actual source. All
11 were fixed, independently verified (fresh worktree, full test suite,
adversarial review of the diff against the claimed fix), and merged into
`main`. **wakil `main` is now at `5d746e0`** — re-install/re-source from
that commit (or later) before testing anything below; testing against an
older checkout will reproduce bugs that are already fixed.

One merge (issue #40, PR #49) had a real conflict against two other already-merged
fixes (issue #36 touched the same function in `_build_stub_entities`, issue
#44 touched the same `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`) — resolved by hand,
re-tested, and confirmed both sets of logic coexist correctly. Worth an
extra-skeptical look if you retest anything touching `_build_stub_entities`
or entity-creation warnings, precisely because it was a hand merge rather
than a clean auto-merge.

## `status` field meaning (all 114 entries now have one)

- **`fixed`** (24 entries) — already confirmed resolved by a prior
  confirmation pass. Leave alone unless you find new contradicting evidence.
- **`ready to be confirmed`** (85 entries) — a relevant wakil fix is now
  merged into `main`; re-test against current `main` and update status/add
  a feedback comment based on what you find.
- **`open`** (5 entries: ids 4, 10, 47, 51, 94) — genuinely unaddressed.
  No merged PR touches these root causes. Re-testing them will reproduce the
  original bug; that's expected, not a regression. See "Known gaps" below
  before spending time re-confirming these — the root cause is already
  understood and just hasn't been fixed yet.

## Issue → PR → `ISSUES.jsonl` id mapping

| GitHub issue | PR (merged) | Root cause | `ISSUES.jsonl` ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| #36 duplicate entity files | #51 | `_build_stub_entities` now suppresses a create-resolution whose subject matches `proposed_note`'s own name/title, or an already-applied `entity_updates` target | 1,6,9,11,15,16,17,28,33,43,45,50,59,63,71,73,76,77,82,92,96–107,113 |
| #37 note path validation | #56 | `validate_proposal`/`_sanitize_note` now check the primary note's path against its type's `schema.directory` and re-slugify an inconsistent filename | 2,5,6,8,12,40,50,54,57,70,74,75,77 |
| #38 schema type suppression | #47 | kb-local schema can now declare `disabled: true` to remove a built-in type from the effective catalog entirely, not just redefine it | 7,9,17,18,26,27,44,45,49,55,62,78,80,88,108,109,113 |
| #39 EntityRevision confidence | #52 | `EntityRevision` gained a `confidence` field — **update path only**, see caveat below | 20,21,22,23 |
| #40 index/list source visibility | #49 | directory-less-type creates (e.g. `index`) now warn instead of silently vanishing, and no longer hard-stop the whole apply | 14,83,85 |
| #41 schema validate command | #54 | new `wakil schema validate <path>` CLI command, reusing `validate_frontmatter` | 77,114 |
| #42 embed syntax docs | #48 | `note-conformance/SKILL.md` now documents `![[target|alias]]` argument order | 12 |
| #43 attachment/URL preservation | #50 | `article`/`text`/`transcript`/`content-synthesis` SKILL.md now instruct preserving inline attachments and raw URLs | 13,24,30,42,46,48,52,56,58,68,72,81,86,87,93 |
| #44 visible skip signal | #55 | `prepare_enrichment` now warns explicitly when a source produces zero files | 19,29,31,32,34,35,36,39,41,53,60,61,64,65,66,69,79,91,95,110,111 |
| #45 stub content visibility | #57 | warns when an update declines to populate an entity that's still on placeholder stub content | 89,90,91,95,112 |
| #46 fabricated content grounding | #53 | `compiled-truth-timeline.md`'s "Open threads" section now has explicit grounding guidance | 25 |

## Caveats to re-test carefully, not just re-run

- **#39 / ids 20–23** (status-inference-no-confidence-signal): PR #52 added
  `confidence` to `EntityRevision`, which only fires on the **update** path
  (`frontmatter_updates` on an existing page). All four of these entries are
  fresh `action=create` book entities — `EntityResolution.proposed_frontmatter`
  (the create path, feeding `_build_stub_entities`) still carries no
  confidence signal. Expect these to still reproduce the original defect;
  that's a known, scoped-down gap, not a broken fix. A new `open` feedback
  comment on each explains this — the prior `closed` comment is stale,
  pre-merge evidence.
- **id=3** (stray-source-file, not covered by any filed issue): bumped to
  `ready to be confirmed` speculatively — #36's subject-based stub
  suppression is plausibly relevant to the `type: source` stray-duplicate
  risk this entry describes, but no test specifically targets this exact
  scenario. Worth an actual repro attempt rather than assuming it's fixed.

## Known gaps (the 5 `open` entries — no fix exists yet)

- **ids 4, 10** (dropped-content-empty-stub on a *fresh* create): root cause
  confirmed unchanged — `_build_stub_entities` still calls the hardcoded
  empty `_stub_content()` on every `action=create`, and none of the 11
  merged fixes touch initial-creation synthesis (only #45 warns on
  *subsequent* update passes against an already-stubbed entity — irrelevant
  here since a single-source book is never revisited).
- **id=47** (timeline-placeholder-not-filled): `_insert_timeline_entry`
  still inserts whatever heading text the model generates verbatim, no
  fallback to the source's captured date. Not filed as an issue; no fix.
- **id=51** (frontmatter-quoting-inconsistency): `metadata['updated'] = today`
  is a plain str that `yaml.safe_dump` quotes, while `created` survives
  as a parsed date object and stays unquoted. Not filed as an issue; no fix.
- **id=94** (raw-capture-filename-ignores-title): `_LEADING_DATE_RE.sub` runs
  twice in the capture path and both passes strip a bare-date filename to
  empty, falling back to `"untitled"`. Was originally judged an intentional
  ADR-0010 tradeoff; the confirming pass found a real root cause contradicting
  that. Not filed as an issue; no fix.

def _suppress_stubs_matching_updates(proposal: EnrichmentProposal) -> None:
    """Drop a create-resolution's stub when its subject already has a home
    via an entity update (DAG node 3) computed in this same proposal.

    Extraction/entity-resolution proposing a create is independent of
    entity-resolution's own update resolutions — a source can correctly
    merge into an existing long-lived entity's Timeline (entity_updates) and
    *also* independently propose a "create" for the same subject under a
    different (often builtin) type, e.g. journal/meeting. Matching against
    the applied entity_updates (rather than every action=update resolution)
    keeps this conservative: an update that entity-resolution proposed but
    that turned out to warrant no real content change is not treated as
    "already has a home."
    """
    if not proposal.entity_updates or not proposal.stub_entities:
        return

    updated_paths = {update.target_note_path for update in proposal.entity_updates}
    # Subject identity for each applied update: the update target's own file
    # stem, plus the name entity-resolution used for the matching resolution
    # (they can differ, e.g. a display name vs. an already-slugified path).
    updated_slugs = {slugify(Path(path).stem) for path in updated_paths}
    for resolution in proposal.entity_resolutions:
        if resolution.action == "update" and resolution.target_note_path in updated_paths:
            updated_slugs.add(slugify(resolution.name))

    kept: list[ProposedFile] = []
    for stub in proposal.stub_entities:
        if slugify(Path(stub.path).stem) in updated_slugs:
            proposal.warnings.append(
                f"{stub.path}: subject already updated via an existing entity in this "
                "same proposal — not creating a duplicate page"
            )
            continue
        kept.append(stub)
    proposal.stub_entities = kept

# note-revision

`content-synthesis` writes a new note from scratch. `note-conformance` checks
a note's shape once it's written. `note-revision` is the step in between,
for the case those two don't cover: a note **already exists**, and new
information — from `entity-enrichment`, `knowledge-research`, a fresh
source, or a user correction — needs to land on it without erasing what's
already there. Losing previously-captured knowledge while "updating" a page
is the single worst failure mode this skill exists to prevent.

## When to use

- New facts about a person, company, project, or topic arrive and a note
  for that subject already exists.
- Explicitly asked to update, revise, or merge new information into an
  existing note.
- An attached companion document (a prep note, an agenda) itself needs
  updating after the fact — e.g. checking off its own open questions in
  place once a meeting resolved them. `transcript` only writes that
  resolution into the *new* meeting note; updating the companion document
  itself is a merge into an existing note, which is this skill's job.
- **Not** for creating a note that doesn't exist yet — that's
  `content-synthesis`. Not for fixing frontmatter/slug/link shape with no
  new information to merge — that's `note-conformance`. If a revision also
  needs a fresh routing decision (the subject moved directories, a new
  entity was split out), hand that off to `note-routing`; don't decide it
  here. And don't assume a newly-mentioned entity (a spun-out company, a
  person who wasn't tracked before) clears the notability gate just because
  it's related to the note you're revising — that judgment belongs to
  `entity-resolution`; name it rather than deciding notability yourself.

## Procedure

- [ ] Step 1: **Read the existing note in full before writing anything.**
      Load its current State, Timeline, and frontmatter. You cannot
      classify a change as additive, contradicting, or duplicate against
      content you haven't read.
- [ ] Step 2: **Re-read the raw source for the new facts, not your memory
      of it.** See "Extraction integrity" below — never transcribe a
      figure, date, or quote from earlier in a conversation when the saved
      raw source is available to re-read at the moment of writing.
- [ ] Step 3: **Classify the new material** against what's already on the
      page: additive, contradicting/superseding, or a duplicate. See "The
      three-tier dedup heuristic" below.
- [ ] Step 4: **Apply the region-specific update discipline**:
      re-synthesize State, append to Timeline. Never regenerate the whole
      page from only the new source. See "State vs. Timeline" below.
- [ ] Step 5: **Diff your draft against the current page before saving.**
      If the new version is shorter, or drops a fact/frontmatter key that
      was there before, stop — you are very likely clobbering, not
      updating. See "The clobbering bug" below.
- [ ] Step 6: **Preview, don't auto-apply.** Surface the diff for
      confirmation before writing, the same as every other wakil write
      path. See "Preview before writing" below.
- [ ] Step 7: **Update provenance**, including the `updated:` frontmatter
      field, and hand off to `note-conformance` for a shape check before
      `kb-commit`.

## State vs. Timeline: two disciplines, one page

A knowledge page has two regions with opposite update disciplines. Get this
backwards and you clobber the page:

- **State (Compiled Truth)** is *re-synthesized* on every update to cover
  the union of what was already there plus the new facts. "Rewrite the
  State section" means re-derive it from everything known, never replace it
  with only the newest source.
- **Timeline (Log)** is *append-only*. New dated entries are added; existing
  entries — including auto-generated back-link lines — are never deleted,
  rewritten, or reordered.

Losing a previously synthesized fact is a regression, not an update.

## The clobbering bug

A cautionary case from a prior system, in outline: three related pages (a
company, a person, and a program) were each fully regenerated from a single
new transcript instead of merged into their existing content. "Rewrite the
State section" was misread as "replace the page with the newest source,"
and the regeneration silently deleted frontmatter, prior distilled history,
and Timeline entries that didn't happen to appear in that one transcript.

The lesson: full-file regeneration is the *mechanism* that enables
clobbering. Prefer surgical edits — append a Timeline entry, edit the State
block — over rewriting an existing page wholesale. Treat "my new version is
shorter than the old one" as a stop-and-check signal, not something to wave
through.

## The three-tier dedup heuristic

Before merging a new fact into an existing note (especially a
tracker-style note that accumulates dated entries — updates, figures,
events), classify it against what's already recorded:

1. **Exact match** (same subject, same date, same value) → it's a
   duplicate. Skip it; don't append a second entry for the same fact.
2. **Fuzzy match** (same subject, same date, a similar-but-not-identical
   value) → flag for review rather than silently picking one. This is
   often a correction or a rounding difference, not a new fact — don't
   guess which.
3. **Conflicting value** (same subject, same date, a materially different
   value) → add it with an explicit note that it conflicts with the
   existing entry. Never silently overwrite the earlier figure and never
   silently drop the new one.

Only tier 1 is safe to resolve automatically. Tiers 2 and 3 are exactly the
kind of ambiguity that "Preview before writing" (below) exists to surface —
report the conflict, cite both entries, and let the confirmation step
decide.

## Resolving conflicting sources

When merging facts that come from more than one source, and they disagree,
apply source precedence rather than picking arbitrarily — highest authority
first: (1) the user's direct statements, (2) the note's existing
State (its current synthesized understanding), (3) Timeline entries (raw
evidence already on the page), (4) external sources (API enrichment, web
search). When two sources genuinely conflict, note the contradiction with
both citations in the Timeline — never silently resolve it by picking one.

Attribute each claim to whoever actually said or clearly implied it, not
whoever it's about. When a founder describes their own company's numbers,
the holder of that claim is the founder, not the company — companies don't
speak, their employees do. A self-reported figure is written as
self-reported, not elevated to verified fact just because it's now the
newest entry on the page.

## Extraction integrity

Never trust working memory for a figure, amount, date, or quote you're
about to write onto a page. If the fact came from a saved raw source
(an ingested transcript, article, or captured email), re-read it from that
file at the moment of writing rather than recalling it from earlier in the
conversation — long-context recall degrades and transposes digits in ways
that silently corrupt exactly the kind of data this skill exists to merge
carefully.

## Preview before writing

Findings and proposed merges are informational until confirmed — this skill
never auto-applies a revision, the same way the rest of wakil's write path
never does. `ingest_service.py`'s enrichment DAG and
`schema_migrate_service.py`'s migration planner both split into a
plan/propose phase that touches nothing and a separate apply phase that
only runs after confirmation (`schema_migrate_service` even re-reads each
file immediately before writing and skips any file that changed since
planning, rather than overwriting it blind). Follow the same shape here:
produce the diff, show what's additive vs. what's flagged as a conflict,
and only write once that's confirmed.

## Provenance and timestamps

- Update the `updated:` frontmatter field (present on identity-type schemas
  such as `person`/`company`, alongside `created:`) when a revision lands —
  don't leave it stale after a real content change.
- Never invent or leave a placeholder date. If the new fact's date isn't
  known, say so explicitly rather than writing "recently" or today's date
  as a guess.
- Never replace a developed note with a freshly generated summary, even
  when the summary is accurate — a shorter, cleaner-looking page that drops
  prior detail is the clobbering bug wearing a different outfit.

Once the merge is written and confirmed, hand off to `note-conformance` for
the shape/schema pass, then `kb-commit` to land it.

## Problem

Following #40 and #44 (both merged), `entity-resolve/SKILL.md` now tells the model: "a source with real, attributable content about a single entity... clears the bar even when the content is thin. Create a minimal stub rather than skip it." A second confirmation round found this guidance is satisfied in a way nobody intended: instead of creating the source's actual best-fit domain entity (e.g. `hobby-project` for a build reference), the model frequently proposes a **redundant `type: source, action: create` self-mirror** of the very source being enriched, landing outside `sources/clippings/` (`source.yaml`'s `directory` is `sources`, not `sources/clippings`).

This is functionally a no-op dressed up as output: `_build_stub_entities` happily builds the stub (schema is valid, directory is valid), so it looks like the fix worked (a file gets written, `#44`'s "nothing will be written" warning never fires) — but the actual intended entity (a hobby-project, hobby-concept, etc.) still never gets created, and there's now a second, junk file for one source that already has a proper raw capture under `sources/clippings/`.

Confirmed by direct reproduction across 11 `ISSUES.jsonl` entries, several with the stray file appearing **alongside** an otherwise-correctly-deduped primary entity (not just replacing a decline):

- id=34 (`Craftsman side table`): "Entity resolution produced only a type=source self-referential 'create'... 1 file was written, but it is `sources/craftsman-side-table-plan-rockler.md`, a 19-line boilerplate stub... The #44 fix's whole-proposal warning never fires here because this junk self-create counts as non-empty output, masking that the intended hobby-project note still never gets written."
- id=11 (`Understanding Wood`): "the originally-reported book/book duplicate no longer occurs... but the enrich still wrote a second, near-empty extraneous file this run — a stray `sources/2026-07-27-understanding-wood-highlights.md` entity-resolution create (type: source) outside `sources/clippings/`... isn't caught by #36's identity check at all [different subject/type]."
- id=45 (`Gibson Chair`): "the primary note was correctly classified... with no duplicate hobby-project file... But entity-resolution again independently created a stray, empty `sources/now-available-make-a-gibson-chair.md` entity."
- id=77 (`SketchUp`): the invalid-name-field half of this record is a false positive (see notes below), but "a redundant `type: source` stub `sources/sketchup-bookmark-reference.md` was created outside `sources/clippings/` despite the content already being captured as a proper source."

Full id list: 3, 11, 34, 39, 45, 61, 64, 69, 76, 77, 79.

## Fix direction

Two complementary layers, matching how #36/#40 were fixed:

1. **`entity-resolve/SKILL.md`**: add explicit guidance that `type: source, action: create` is never the right answer for the source currently being enriched — it's already captured as the raw file under `sources/clippings/`; re-proposing it as its own entity is inherently redundant. When the "don't skip the source's own subject" guidance applies, the model must identify the *actual* best-fit domain type for that subject (matching the migration/category context and existing sibling entities), not fall back to mirroring the source itself.
2. **Code-level backstop** (`_build_stub_entities` or `_run_entity_resolution`, `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`): treat a create-resolution with `entity_type == "source"` for the entity currently being enriched as a structural no-op — suppress it (with a warning distinguishing it from a legitimate skip), the same way #36 suppresses a create that duplicates `proposed_note`'s own subject. A source can never legitimately need to re-create itself as an entity; if entity-resolution proposes this, it's evidence the intended domain entity was never actually decided, and that should be surfaced as a warning, not a silently "successful" write.

#38 (PR #47) fixed the case where entity-resolution proposes a **built-in** type that a vault's kb-local schema never uses. A second confirmation round found a distinct, unfixed routing gap between **two equally valid kb-local types**, which #38's mechanism was never meant to address: reference-material sources within a specific craft/hobby category still get classified as the reading-category `book`/`article` type instead of the craft-category `hobby-concept`, even when a directly analogous sibling source in the same folder was correctly routed to `hobby-concept`.

Confirmed by direct reproduction — the model isn't leaking a suppressed builtin here (`book` has no wakil builtin equivalent at all, it's kb-local-only, so #38's `disabled: true` mechanism is structurally inapplicable regardless of configuration):

- id=26 (`Anarchist's Tool Chest`): "wakil proposed `type: book`, `reading/books/...` instead of `hobby-concept`... `book` has no wakil builtin equivalent... so PR #47's built-in-suppression mechanism is structurally [inapplicable]."
- id=27 (`Anarchist's Workbench`, sibling case): same result, "identical to the original defect."
- id=80 (`The Joiner and Cabinet Maker`): same result, "the underlying wrong-type behavior is unchanged."
- id=49 (`Japanese Toolbox`, a full third-party instructional article rather than a bare reference PDF): "wakil again classified it as `type: article` in `reading/articles/`, exactly matching the prior confirmation pass's finding... not `hobby-concept`."

## Fix direction

Add guidance to `entity-resolve/SKILL.md` (and/or `note-routing/SKILL.md`, whichever governs this decision) instructing the model to weigh the source's own migration/category context and sibling-note precedent more heavily when two valid kb-local types could both fit: reference material (a bare PDF excerpt, a third-party instructional article) that lives within a specific craft/hobby-project category, with no personal reading record attached, should route to that category's own reference type (`hobby-concept`) rather than defaulting to the reading-category type just because the content resembles a book/article. Point explicitly at checking for sibling notes already resolved this way in the same directory as a strong signal, since that precedent already exists in these vaults and isn't being used reliably.

Two earlier merged fixes changed src/wakil/skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md: #40 added guidance to recognize index/list-shaped sources, and #44 added "a source with real, attributable content about a single entity... clears the bar even when the content is thin. A second confirmation round found the model satisfies "create a minimal stub" by proposing a REDUNDANT entity_type: "source", action: "create" for the very source being enriched -- mirroring content that already exists as the raw capture under sources/clippings/ (source.yaml's schema.directory is "sources", not "sources/clippings", so this lands as a stray file outside the normal convention). This looks like a fix (a nonzero file gets written, #44's "nothing will be written" warning from ingest_service.py never fires) but is a structural no-op: the actual intended domain entity (hobby-project, hobby-concept, etc. depending on the vault) still never gets created.

Confirmed real-world reproductions, several where this happens ALONGSIDE an otherwise-correctly-deduped primary entity (not just replacing a decline):
- A source about a specific woodworking build (title + bare single link) resolved to only a type=source self-mirror create (a 19-line boilerplate stub under sources/), never a hobby-project entity for the actual build.
- A source whose primary book-duplicate was correctly suppressed (by #36's fix) still separately spawned a stray sources/<slug>-highlights.md (type: source) file.
- A source correctly classified as hobby-project with no duplicate hobby-project file still separately spawned a stray sources/<slug>.md (type: source) entity.

## Fix direction

Two complementary layers:

1. src/wakil/skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md: add explicit guidance, right where the "create a minimal stub rather than skip it" text already is, that entity_type: source is NEVER the right answer for the source currently being enriched -- it's already captured as the raw file; re-proposing it as its own entity is inherently redundant. When this "don't skip the source's own subject" guidance applies, the model must identify the actual best-fit domain type for that subject, not fall back to mirroring the source itself. Keep the addition small and in the same voice as the surrounding text; this file is lint-checked (tests/unit/test_skill_lint.py) -- run the full suite to confirm you haven't broken it (line-count ceiling, no dangling cross-references).
2. Code-level backstop in src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py (read _run_entity_resolution, _build_stub_entities, and EnrichmentProposal.source_id first): a create-resolution with entity_type == "source" should be treated as a structural no-op for the entity currently being enriched and suppressed -- with a warning distinguishing this from a legitimate skip (e.g. naming the resolution and noting the intended domain entity was likely never decided), mirroring how #36's fix (_proposed_note_subject_slug / suppression in _build_stub_entities) already suppresses a create that duplicates proposed_note's own subject. Add unit tests in tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py (read it first for existing patterns around _build_stub_entities, EnrichmentProposal, proposal.warnings) covering: a create-resolution for entity_type="source" gets suppressed with a warning rather than producing a stub; a create-resolution for a genuinely different, legitimate domain type (e.g. hobby-project, person) is unaffected (no regression).

2. Implement the smallest correct fix per the direction above.
3. Add/update tests.
4. Run uv sync, uv run ruff check ., uv run pytest -q (including skill-lint) -- all must pass.
5. Branch fix/issue-58-source-self-mirror-suppression. Commit with a gitmoji-prefixed Conventional Commits message, trailer "Fixes #58", ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>".
6. Push and open a PR via gh pr create against ebridges/wakil referencing #58. Capture PR number/URL.
7. Return the structured result.

Note: issues #59, #60, #61, #62 (separate concurrent agents/worktrees) may also touch ingest_service.py and/or entity-resolve/SKILL.md -- a merge conflict when the user merges more than one PR is expected and fine.`, { isolation: 'worktree', schema: FIX_SCHEMA })

(' (PR ' + fix.pr_url + ')') : (' (no PR reported -- check gh pr list --repo ebridges/wakil --head ' + fix.branch + ')')}. Independently verify -- don't trust the self-report.

  name: 'fix-wakil-issue-60',
  description: 'Fix wakil #60: dated journal/meeting creates not suppressed against same-proposal updates',
  phases: [{ title: 'Fix' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
}

const FIX_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    branch: { type: 'string' },
    pr_number: { type: 'number' },
    pr_url: { type: 'string' },
    tests_passed: { type: 'boolean' },

    summary: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['branch', 'tests_passed', 'lint_passed', 'summary'],
}
const VERIFY_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed_good', 'needs_followup'] },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['verdict', 'notes'],
}

phase('Fix')
const fix = await agent(`You are fixing GitHub issue #60 on ebridges/wakil (a local-first Python CLI agent for a Markdown knowledge base). You're in a fresh git worktree checked out from the CURRENT main (already includes 11 previously merged fixes, #36-46). Read CLAUDE.md first: keep this diff small and conservative, matching the existing suppression logic's own cautious style.

## Issue #60: dated journal/meeting creates aren't suppressed when the same source already updates an accumulating entity

_suppress_stubs_matching_updates (src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py -- read it in full now, along with _build_stub_entities and _proposed_note_subject_slug right above it) drops a create-resolution's stub when its SUBJECT SLUG matches an applied entity_updates target's slug. This correctly catches "create and update propose the same-named subject," but cannot catch a dated single-occurrence record (journal/meeting) whose own name/slug is necessarily different from the accumulating project entity its content is ALSO being merged into -- e.g. a journal entry titled "2014-05-17 Elektrum VPC Subnet Layout Finalized" (slug elektrum-work-vpc-subnet-layout-finalized) will never slug-match the project it's about (hobbies/elektrum.md, slug elektrum), even though both represent the SAME source's content landing twice.

Confirmed by direct reproduction across 12 dated elektrum journal entries: each time, entity resolution correctly proposed an UPDATE to hobbies/elektrum.md's Timeline via entity_updates, but ALSO independently created a separate, empty journal/<date-topic-slug>.md duplicate -- the exact same mechanism (_suppress_stubs_matching_updates's slug-matching) confirmed not to fire for any of them, since the journal entry's own slug is topic/date-specific and structurally never equals "elektrum".

A related, RESOLVER-violating variant: entity-resolution also invents a brand-new meetings/ entity duplicating an ALREADY-EXISTING (not same-proposal) journal entry, contradicting this vault's RESOLVER.md rule 4 ("don't invent a meetings/ directory before it's needed... log under... a journal entry"). Note: for this specific vault this is now mitigated by a kb-local disabled:true marker suppressing the meeting builtin entirely -- but the underlying entity-resolution/RESOLVER-precedence gap is real and vault-independent, so still worth the SKILL.md guidance fix below.

## Fix direction

1. Extend _suppress_stubs_matching_updates (or add a parallel check applied at the same point in _run_entity_resolution, right after _run_entity_updates runs) so that, when proposal.entity_updates is non-empty (this exact source already correctly merged into SOME existing accumulating entity in this same proposal), a create-resolution for a SINGLE-OCCURRENCE-SHAPED type whose sole purpose is recording "what happened via this source" is suppressed as redundant -- matching by "this source already has a home via an update in this same proposal," NOT by subject-name-slug. Scope this narrowly to the "journal" and "meeting" entity types specifically (not the whole single-occurrence page_shape category) to avoid over-suppressing a legitimate case like a personal "reflection" entity that could be genuinely distinct from a project's factual Timeline even when sharing a source. Read load_entity_schemas/schema.page_shape (src/wakil/schema/loader.py) if you need to check a resolution's type's page_shape. Add a warning distinguishing this suppression from other cases, matching the existing warning style in _suppress_stubs_matching_updates.

All already `ready to be confirmed` — no `ISSUES.jsonl` update needed, they're correctly flagged for the next confirmation round now that the code is actually merged.

## Round 2 complete

All 5 new issues (#58–#62) fixed, independently verified, and merged into `main` (now `14938d4`) — **zero merge conflicts this time**, even though 4 of the 5 touched `entity-resolve/SKILL.md` and 2 touched `ingest_service.py`, because each fix agent deliberately inserted at distinct, non-overlapping locations (confirmed by the verifiers checking against the other in-flight branches before finishing).

| Issue | PR | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| #58 stray `type:source` self-mirror | [#66](https://github.com/ebridges/wakil/pull/66) | New `_is_source_self_mirror` check suppresses a redundant self-referential source create; SKILL.md guidance to pick the real domain type instead |
| #59 note-revision attachment gap | [#65](https://github.com/ebridges/wakil/pull/65) | Attachment/URL guidance added to the update/merge path; embed paths now required vault-root-absolute; sibling-attachment boundary documented |
| #60 dated journal/meeting duplicates | [#67](https://github.com/ebridges/wakil/pull/67) | New `_suppress_dated_record_stubs_matching_updates`, scoped to journal/meeting, matching by same-proposal update rather than fragile slug comparison |
| #61 near-duplicate name variants | [#63](https://github.com/ebridges/wakil/pull/63) | SKILL.md guidance only (no fuzzy-match code, as scoped) |
| #62 category-context routing | [#64](https://github.com/ebridges/wakil/pull/64) | SKILL.md guidance to weigh sibling precedent over defaulting to the reading-category type |

One thing worth noting from #58's verify pass: a minor, non-blocking edge case remains in the self-mirror heuristic (a contrived prefix-substring case could theoretically misfire) — not one of the actually-reported instances, so I didn't chase it further, but flagging for awareness.

`ISSUES.jsonl` needed no changes — all 32 affected ids were already `ready to be confirmed`, correctly positioned for the next confirmation pass against current `main`.

Read /Users/ebridges/Projects/kb-personal/ISSUES.jsonl for full context — 115 tracked issues from repeated confirmation passes against wakil (currently at commit 14938d4, after issues #36–46 and #58–62 were fixed and merged). 82 are "fixed", 3 are "closed" (not actionable — see their feedback for why, don't reopen), and 30 are "open" — every one has been freshly re-confirmed this session with a live reproduction and/or direct code citation, so treat the feedback array's most recent entry per id as ground truth, not stale.

File GitHub issues, fix, and merge in priority order below. After each merge, note the commit SHA and issue/PR numbers so the next confirmation pass can target the right ids — same handoff format as WAKIL-FIXES-2026-07-27.md in the repo.

## Priority 1 — highest-impact, broadest-reach

A. Dated-record duplicate creation bypasses the #60 fix entirely (ids 96–107, 12 issues, all high severity)
Root cause, code-confirmed and live-reproduced repeatedly: in ingest_service.py, proposal.proposed_note is set by the extraction step (~line 683) before entity resolution runs. Both _suppress_stubs_matching_updates (line 1088) and _suppress_dated_record_stubs_matching_updates (line 1137, the #60/PR#67 fix) only ever prune proposal.stub_entities/proposal.entity_resolutions — neither one ever inspects or nulls proposal.proposed_note. So when extraction independently decides a dated journal-style source is "worth a durable note," it writes a duplicate entity alongside a perfectly correct Timeline update to the real project entity, and #60's fix structurally cannot catch it because it's checking the wrong field. Fix direction: extend the suppression check (or add a new one) to also compare proposal.proposed_note's subject/slug against proposal.entity_updates targets, same logic as the existing functions, just applied to the field they're currently missing.

B. RESOLVER-precedence deferral failure — dated meeting should defer to existing journal entry (id=113, medium)
A different, cross-proposal variant of the same theme: when a dated journal/YYYY/ entry already exists for an event (e.g. a contractor call), and a separate source describing the same event gets ingested later, entity resolution should defer to the existing entry per RESOLVER.md rule #4 — instead it invents a new entity every time, and which wrong destination it picks has now varied across three confirmation rounds (meetings/ → project/ → people/). This is not the same bug as (A) — it's not an intra-proposal duplicate, it's a failure to search/prefer an existing same-day entity across proposals. Needs its own fix, likely in whatever step decides create-vs-defer for a new source, checking existing dated entries for the same date/subject before proposing a new entity at all.

C. Fresh entity creation never synthesizes source content — _stub_content() hardcoded placeholder (ids 4, 10, high)
_build_stub_entities always calls _stub_content() for any action=create entity resolution, which returns a literal hardcoded empty template ("_Synthesized current state — rewrite when facts change._") regardless of how much real content the source actually contains (Kindle highlights, technique writeups, etc.). This is the most severe remaining content-fidelity gap — it's why every fresh-create note needs manual authoring. Not touched by any of the 16 merged fixes so far (they all target the update/revision path or entity-resolution typing, never the synthesis-on-create step itself). Fix direction: _stub_content() needs to actually invoke synthesis (the same mechanism _run_entity_updates/note-revision uses) rather than returning a fixed string.

## Priority 2 — real gaps, moderate impact

D. No landing entity for index/list-shaped sources (ids 83, 85, medium)
A source that's itself an index of other entities (e.g. a project-list or reading-list file linking ~20 other pages) resolves to the builtin index type, which has no schema.directory to route into — so it silently (well, now visibly, per #40's warning fix) produces 0 files and no landing entity. Fix direction: either give index sources a real destination (a generic drafts/-style catch-all, or let kb-local schemas declare an index-shaped type the way hobby-concept etc. already exist), or make entity-resolution route index content into whatever type fits (e.g. hobby-concept for a woodworking project list) rather than defaulting to the dead-end builtin.

E. Field-level status inference has no confidence signal, and it's CREATE-path only (ids 20–23, low, but architectural)
EntityRevision.confidence (added by #39/PR#52) is wired only into _run_entity_updates (the update path). EntityResolution.proposed_frontmatter, which is what _build_stub_entities uses for a fresh action=create book/article, is a plain dict with no per-field confidence anywhere. A book's status: finished gets asserted with the same confidence whether it's backed by one early highlight or a full read-through. Fix direction: extend whatever mechanism produces EntityRevision.confidence to also run against proposed_frontmatter on the create path, or add a lighter per-field confidence dict there.

F. Entity-resolution and page-synthesis can disagree, synthesis wins (id=115, medium, newly discovered — not yet filed)
With sibling hobby-concept precedents present, entity-resolution now correctly proposes type: hobby-concept for a third-party instructional article (confidence 0.90) — but the synthesis stage that follows ignores that decision and writes type: article anyway. This is a genuinely new bug surfaced by #62's own fix working correctly at the resolution stage while a downstream stage doesn't honor it. Fix direction: whatever stage does final type/path selection during synthesis needs to read from the resolution's decision rather than re-deriving type independently.

G. "Whose build is this" signal still not reliably driving hobby-project vs hobby-concept classification (id=49, medium)
Across 3 confirmation rounds this has landed on 3 different wrong answers for the same content (misfiled as article, then a resolution/synthesis mismatch — see F above, which was discovered testing this exact id — then reverted to hobby-project). The underlying signal ("is this the user's own in-progress build, or a third-party article describing someone else's build") isn't being captured deterministically anywhere in the prompt/resolution logic. Fix direction: probably needs explicit instruction in entity-resolve/SKILL.md naming this exact distinction, since #62's sibling-precedent guidance alone isn't sufficient — it only helps when a matching precedent already exists, not when reasoning about the source's own voice/perspective.

H. Hand-authored multi-date reflective journal never uses the builtin journal type (id=14, high)
A two/three-date personal reflection (discussing external works in passing) gets split into 2-3 empty stub entities for the works mentioned, never landing as an actual journal entry — 100% of the real reflective content is lost. Reproduced consistently across all rounds with zero variance. Fix direction: entity-resolution needs a stronger signal for "this source's primary subject is the author's own first-person reflection, not the things it references" — likely needs explicit guidance alongside whatever handles #62's category-context routing, since it's the same class of "whose content is this really about" question.

## Priority 3 — low-severity, mostly cosmetic

I. Book title/slug carries the full marketing subtitle (ids 2, 5, low)
title: "11/22/63: A Novel" instead of "11/22/63"; slug/title generation for document-category types (book/article) is entirely model-chosen with no code-level subtitle-stripping. Consistent 3/3 reproduction across rounds (though which artifact shows it — title vs. filename — varies).

J. Attachment paths on the UPDATE path aren't vault-root-absolute and files never get copied (id=8, low but functionally breaks links)
On a merge/update into an existing entity, new image references get written as literal source-relative paths (not vault-root-absolute per RESOLVER.md), and the referenced files are never copied into the vault — so the resulting ![[...]]/![]() links are always dangling. #59/PR#65 fixed attachment preservation (the reference now survives) but not correctness (the path is wrong and the file doesn't exist).

K. Timeline entries can get a placeholder heading instead of a real date (id=47, medium)
_insert_timeline_entry (ingest_service.py:1027-1038) inserts whatever heading text the model generates verbatim — "### (date not recorded)" or "### Undated — source: clipping" — with no code-level fallback to the source's captured/retrieved date when the source text itself lacks one. Recurred spontaneously in an unrelated test, so it's not source-specific.

L. updated:/created: frontmatter quoting inconsistency (id=51, low)
ingest_service.py:1096 sets metadata['updated'] = today as a plain str, which yaml.safe_dump quotes to disambiguate from a date; created survives as an already-parsed date object from the original frontmatter and stays unquoted. Purely cosmetic but easy fix (cast updated to a date object before dumping, matching created's type).

M. Raw capture filename ignores its own generated title (id=94, low)
When a source file's own filename is just a bare date (e.g. 2014-02-17.md), the raw capture lands as sources/clippings/<date>-untitled.md instead of using the frontmatter title wakil itself generated. Root cause: _LEADING_DATE_RE.sub runs twice in the capture path (once on the origin filename's stem, once again on the slugified result in _build_raw_file, ~lines 260 and 1978) — both passes strip a bare-date filename to empty and fall back to "untitled", independent of the title. Note: this was originally assumed to be an intentional ADR-0010 tradeoff, but a confirming pass found this specific root cause contradicts that assumption — it's a real bug, not a tradeoff.

## Problem

#60 (PR #67, merged) added `_suppress_dated_record_stubs_matching_updates` to catch a journal/meeting create-resolution that duplicates the same source's concurrent update to an accumulating entity — but it only prunes `proposal.stub_entities`/`proposal.entity_resolutions`. It never inspects or nulls `proposal.proposed_note`, which is set independently by the **extraction** step (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, `_run_extraction`, ~line 683) *before* entity resolution ever runs.

When extraction itself decides a dated journal-style source is "worth a durable note" (producing its own `proposed_note`), that note is never suppressed by anything — #60's fix (and #36's `_suppress_stubs_matching_updates` before it) both structurally check the wrong field for this case. The result: a perfectly correct Timeline update to the real project entity lands *alongside* a duplicate note from `proposed_note`, and it reproduces regardless of how many times #60 is re-verified, because #60 was never checking the field where this particular duplicate actually originates.

Confirmed by repeated direct reproduction and code reading across 12 `ISSUES.jsonl` entries — all elektrum dated-journal sources whose content correctly updates `hobbies/elektrum.md`'s Timeline.

Extend the suppression check (or add a parallel one, following the same pattern as #36/#60) to also compare `proposal.proposed_note`'s subject/slug against `proposal.entity_updates` targets — the same logic already used for `stub_entities`, just applied to the field it's currently missing. If `proposed_note`'s own subject matches (or its type is `journal`/`meeting` and this source already produced a real `entity_update` in the same proposal), null it out with a warning, mirroring how #36 already suppresses a duplicate `stub_entities` entry.

This is a distinct, cross-proposal variant of #60's problem: #60 fixed suppression *within one proposal* (the same source producing both an update and a redundant create); this is about a *separate, later* source describing an event that's *already* recorded in an existing entity from an *earlier* proposal.

Confirmed by direct, repeated reproduction: seeding `journal/2024/2024-01-05.md` with a contractor-call entry, then ingesting/enriching a separate meeting-notes source describing the same event, entity resolution fails to defer to the existing journal entry every time — and which wrong destination it invents has varied across three confirmation rounds (`meetings/` → `project/` → `people/`), indicating the model has no reliable signal for "check existing notes for this date/subject before proposing a new entity," not just a wrong-destination bug.

## Fix direction

This is a cross-proposal search/defer problem, not an intra-proposal suppression problem — #60's mechanism cannot address it by construction (it only compares entities within the same `EnrichmentProposal`). Entity-resolution already receives "existing notes provided" as context per `entity-resolve/SKILL.md` (search-hit candidates passed into the resolution prompt) — strengthen the guidance there to explicitly instruct: before proposing `action: create` for a dated record (journal/meeting) describing an event, check the provided existing-notes candidates for one already covering the same date/subject, and defer (`action: update` or `skip`) rather than creating a new entity, regardless of what specific type that new entity would be. Since the *specific* wrong type has varied across rounds while the deferral failure has not, the fix needs to target the defer-vs-create decision itself, not any one destination type.

## Problem

`_build_stub_entities` (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, ~line 891) always calls `_stub_content()` (~line 1268) for any `action=create` entity resolution. `_stub_content()` returns a literal hardcoded placeholder — `_Synthesized current state — rewrite when facts change._` with an empty Timeline — regardless of how much real content the source actually contains (Kindle highlights, technique writeups, full articles). This is the single most severe remaining content-fidelity gap in the pipeline: every fresh-create note reaches disk empty and needs manual authoring, and none of the 16 fixes merged so far touch this — they all target the update/revision path (`_run_entity_updates`, `EntityRevision`) or entity-resolution typing/duplication, never the synthesis-on-create step itself.

Confirmed by direct reproduction: ingesting a synthetic Kindle-highlights-style book note and running `wakil enrich` produced a brand-new entity page whose entire body is the literal hardcoded stub text, even though the real highlights/quotes were fully synthesized elsewhere in the same run (in the — now-suppressed — duplicate `proposed_note`/stub pair from #36's fix, confirming the real content generation capability exists in the pipeline, just not on this path).

## Fix direction

`_stub_content()` needs to actually invoke synthesis — the same mechanism `_run_entity_updates`/`note-revision` already uses to produce `EntityRevision.compiled_truth` from source material — rather than returning a fixed string. Concretely: when `_build_stub_entities` is about to write a stub for a genuine `action=create`, run the source text plus the resolution's `proposed_frontmatter` through the same model-driven synthesis step the update path uses (adapted for "there is no existing content to merge with — this is the first content"), and use that as the stub's initial Compiled Truth/Timeline instead of the placeholder. ## Problem

A source that's itself an index of many other entities (a project-list or reading-list file linking ~20 other pages) resolves entity-resolution to the builtin `index` type, whose schema (`src/wakil/schema/entities/index.yaml`) has `directory: null` — no canonical destination. #40's fix (merged) made this visible (a warning: "type 'index' has no canonical directory to route into") instead of silently vanishing, but the index source itself still never gets a landing entity — it produces 0 files every time.

## Problem

#59 (PR #65, merged) added attachment/URL *preservation* guidance to the update/merge path (`note-revision/SKILL.md`) — the reference to an attachment now survives a merge instead of being collapsed into prose. But a follow-up confirmation found the reference that survives is still wrong in two ways: the embed target path isn't normalized to vault-root-absolute (RESOLVER.md's Linking convention), and the referenced file is never actually copied anywhere — so the resulting link is always dangling. This isn't specific to the update path either: a grep of `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` for any file-copy mechanism (`copy`, `shutil`) returns nothing at all — wakil has never had code to copy an attachment file into a vault destination, on any path.

Confirmed by direct reproduction: setting up a real hobby-project entity with genuine embedded images, then merging a follow-up source with two new image references (twice, in fresh workspaces) — both trials wrote embed paths as the literal source-relative path copied verbatim rather than vault-root-absolute, and no attachment directory/files were ever created, so every link (both the pre-existing and the newly-introduced references) ends up dangling.

## Fix direction

Two parts:
1. **Path normalization**: on the update/merge path, normalize a newly-introduced embed's target path to vault-root-absolute per RESOLVER.md's Linking convention (rule 5: a sibling folder named after the project file) — the same rule #42/#59 already apply to note-conformance's Embeds guidance, just not yet enforced/applied at the point an update actually writes the path.
2. **File copying**: implement the actual copy — when an update introduces a new attachment reference resolvable to a file on disk (e.g. found relative to the source's own raw-capture location), copy it into the destination entity's sibling attachment folder (RESOLVER.md rule 5) rather than only rewriting the reference and leaving the file itself unmoved. Scope this conservatively: only copy files that are unambiguously locatable from the source's own context (its raw capture's sibling directory) — don't attempt to guess or search broadly for a file that isn't clearly co-located with the source.

## Problem

`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py:1352` sets `metadata["updated"] = today` as a plain Python `str`. `yaml.safe_dump` quotes a string that looks like a date to disambiguate it from an actual date scalar, so `updated:` always comes out quoted (`updated: '2026-07-27'`), while `created:` — which survives as an already-parsed `date` object from the original frontmatter round-trip — stays unquoted (`created: 2026-01-15`). Confirmed by direct reproduction twice, merging new content into two different existing entities: the pre-existing unquoted `created:` field stayed unquoted while the freshly-stamped `updated:` came out quoted, every time.

## Fix direction

Cast `today` to an actual `date` object (matching the type `created` already has after its frontmatter round-trip) before assigning it into `metadata`, rather than leaving it as a plain string — so `yaml.safe_dump` treats both fields identically and neither gets quoted.

## Problem

When a source file's own filename is just a bare date (e.g. `2014-02-17.md`), the raw capture lands as `sources/clippings/<date>-untitled.md` instead of using the descriptive title wakil itself generates in the frontmatter. This was originally assumed to be an intentional ADR-0010 tradeoff (the raw capture's filename is deliberately kept independent of the model-generated title, for deterministic, idempotent re-ingest dedup) — a confirming pass this round found a concrete root cause that contradicts that assumption: it's a real bug, not a tradeoff.

Root cause: `_LEADING_DATE_RE.sub` runs **twice** in the capture path — once on the origin filename's own stem (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` ~line 268), and again on the slugified result inside `_build_raw_file` (~line 2313). When the filename is itself only a date, both passes strip it to empty and fall back to the literal string `"untitled"` — independent of whatever descriptive title the model generated for the same capture.

Confirmed by direct reproduction: ingesting a text file named `2014-02-17.md` (matching the original elektrum journal pattern) produced raw capture `sources/clippings/2026-07-27-untitled.md` despite a well-formed generated title (`"2026-07-27 Elektrum AWS VPC Setup Notes"`) sitting right there in the same file's frontmatter.

## Fix direction

De-duplicate the double `_LEADING_DATE_RE.sub` application — the date prefix should only be stripped once (either from the origin filename's stem, or from the already-slugified result, not both) before falling back to `"untitled"`. This preserves ADR 0010's actual intent (a filename basis independent of the model's title) while fixing the specific case where a bare-date filename gets stripped twice into nothing.

Cause: _LEADING_DATE_RE.sub is applied twice in the capture path (once to the origin filename's stem, once again to the slugified result in _build_raw_file, ingest_service.py lines 260 and 1978) -- when the filename is itself only a date, both passes strip it to empty and fall back to the literal string 'untitled', independent of the model-generated title."

# wakil fixes — round 3 (2026-07-27) — confirming-agent brief

Handoff for the agent re-testing `ISSUES.jsonl` entries against the current wakil
install. This is the third round — see `WAKIL-FIXES-2026-07-27.md` for round 1/2
context (issues #36–#46, #58–#62) if you need it, but everything below is
self-contained for round 3.

## What changed

12 GitHub issues (`ebridges/wakil` #68–#79) were filed from round 2's
confirmation feedback, root-caused against wakil's actual source, fixed,
independently verified, and merged into `main`. **wakil `main` is now at
`fb35e83`** — re-install/re-source from that commit or later before testing
anything below.

One issue (item "I" from the original priority list — book title/slug
carrying the Kindle subtitle, ids 2/5) was explicitly **not** filed or fixed:
it directly contradicted standing feedback that wakil using the Kindle-provided
title as-is is correct behavior, not a defect. Ids 2/5 are now marked `wont fix`
in `ISSUES.jsonl` with an explanatory `closed` feedback comment — don't
re-open or re-test these.

Two merges this round required real conflict resolution (not just re-runs):
- **#90 (issue #76)** conflicted with #77's Timeline date-fallback work at the
  exact same call site (`_insert_timeline_entry`) — resolved by combining both:
  the embed-path-normalized `timeline_entry` variable, passed with the
  `fallback_date` parameter.
- **#91 (issue #70)** — the largest, most architecturally significant fix this
  round (real content synthesis on the create path) — hit a 1Password SSH-agent
  lockup mid-commit in its own worktree, sat staged-but-uncommitted, and needed
  a manual rebase onto main (which had moved 7 PRs forward by then) before it
  could even be pushed. Conflicted with #68's `_suppress_proposed_note_matching_updates`
  (both insert a new function/call at the same point in `_run_entity_resolution`) —
  resolved by keeping both functions and running suppression before synthesis
  (so synthesis only fires for stubs/notes that survive all suppression passes).

## `status` field meaning (all 115 entries have one)

- **`fixed`** (82) — confirmed resolved by a prior pass. Leave alone.
- **`ready to be confirmed`** (28) — a relevant wakil fix is now merged into
  `main`; re-test against current `main`.
- **`closed`** (3) — not actionable, won't become "fixed" through re-testing
  (see each one's feedback for why — e.g. an accepted, documented boundary).
  Don't re-open.
- **`wont fix`** (2, ids 2/5) — re-examined and determined not to be a defect
  at all (wakil's Kindle-title-as-is behavior is intentional). Don't re-open,
  don't file a new issue for this.

## Issue → PR → `ISSUES.jsonl` id mapping (round 3)

## Caveats to re-test carefully, not just re-run

- **#76 / id=8**: only the path-normalization half was fixed (embed targets are
  now vault-root-absolute). File copying was explicitly declined as out of
  scope — no mechanism anywhere in wakil copies an attachment file into a vault
  destination, on any path (create or update), and building one would require
  new file-discovery machinery beyond this issue's bounds. Expect the link to
  still be dangling (file doesn't exist at the target path) even though the
  *path itself* is now correct — that's a real, disclosed partial fix, not a
  broken one. A follow-up issue for actual file-copying would need to be filed
  separately if this KB wants it addressed.
- **#73 / id=115**: verifier found one cosmetic, non-blocking issue — when
  `proposed_note`'s frontmatter has no `type:` at all (not just a different
  one), the correction warning reads "Corrected the proposed note's type from

- **#68 / #70 interaction**: both touch the same call site in

  `proposed_note` suppressed as redundant with a same-proposal update, and (b)
  has another stub that survives and should get real synthesized content — to
  confirm the ordering holds up under a realistic combined scenario, since this
  exact combination wasn't separately tested end-to-end beyond each PR's own
  unit tests.
- **#70 is the largest fix in this batch** (a new mandatory model call added to
  the enrich DAG). Worth the most scrutiny of anything here: confirm real
  Kindle-highlight-style content actually gets synthesized into Compiled Truth
  on a fresh create (not just that the placeholder is gone), and confirm a
  genuinely sparse source still degrades to an honest minimal stub rather than
  fabricating content to fill the space.

(the same way id=115 was discovered while re-testing id=49 last round), mark

content.text:
## Round 3 complete

All 12 issues (#68–#79) fixed, independently verified, and merged into `main` (now `fb35e83`, 590 passing tests). GitHub issues auto-closed on merge; `ISSUES.jsonl` updated (28 ids → `ready to be confirmed`, ids 2/5 → `wont fix`).

**Two real conflicts resolved by hand:**
- #90 (#76) conflicted with #77 at the exact same `_insert_timeline_entry` call — combined both (embed-normalized entry + fallback date param).
- #91 (#70, the big content-synthesis fix) hit the same 1Password SSH lockup mid-commit as before, sat staged for a while, then needed a manual rebase onto main (which had moved 7 PRs since) — conflicted with #68 at the same call site in `_run_entity_resolution`; resolved by keeping both new functions and ordering suppression before synthesis.

**One process mistake I caught and fixed**: I skipped merging PR #89 (#79) partway through and moved on — caught it during final verification (open-PR list wasn't empty) and merged it before finishing.

**Handoff document**: `WAKIL-FIXES-2026-07-27-round3.md` in `kb-personal`, same format as round 1/2's brief — full issue→PR→id mapping, and specific caveats flagged for careful re-testing rather than a rubber-stamp pass:
- **#76/id=8**: only path-normalization was fixed; file-copying was explicitly and correctly declined as out of scope (still-dangling links expected, but the path itself is now correct).
- **#68+#70 interaction**: worth a combined repro (a source that both suppresses a redundant `proposed_note` *and* triggers real synthesis on a surviving stub) since that exact combination wasn't tested end-to-end.
- **#70 itself**: the largest fix this round (new mandatory model call on the create path) — deserves the most scrutiny of anything here.

Next round of review, we're only 8 issues away from a clear run!

Read /Users/ebridges/Projects/kb-personal/ISSUES.jsonl for full context — 116 tracked issues, now at wakil commit fb35e83 after issues #36–46, #58–62, and #68–79 were fixed and merged across three confirmation rounds. 106 are resolved (103 fixed, 3 closed — not actionable, don't reopen — plus 2 wont fix, ids 2/5, confirmed intentional behavior). 8 are open and need fixing. All 8 have been freshly re-tested this round with live reproduction and/or direct code citations — treat each id's feedback array's most recent entry as ground truth.

A. New root cause behind the "index" gap (ids 83, 85, plus new id=116) — file this one first

Round 3's #71 fix (sibling-precedent routing for index-shaped sources) actually works — entity-resolution now correctly types a project-list or reading-list source as hobby-project/hobby-concept instead of the dead-end builtin index. But #73's _correct_proposed_note_type (which retypes a proposed_note to match entity-resolution's decision) only swaps type: and moves the file path — it never reconciles the frontmatter to the new type's required fields. When the old and new types have different schemas (e.g. index's title/tags/created vs. hobby-project's name/craft/status/updated), the corrected note fails schema validation and nothing gets written — the exact same 0-files symptom ids 83/85 originally reported, just via a new mechanism one layer downstream. Fix direction: _correct_proposed_note_type needs to backfill/derive the target type's required fields (not just relabel), the same way _build_stub_entities already does for a fresh stub — or route through that existing field-population logic instead of doing a bare type swap.

B. Status-inference confidence still doesn't reach book/article creation (ids 20–23, low severity but architectural)

#72's new EntityResolution.proposed_frontmatter_confidence field is wired only into _build_stub_entities (secondary/referenced stub entities) — never into extraction.proposed_note, which is what actually gets used to create a fresh book or article. Code-confirmed: the dataclass docstring for the new field explicitly excludes proposed_note, saying "the concept doesn't apply" there — but that's precisely the path where an uncertain status: finished/reading inference matters most (a book status guessed from a single early Kindle highlight). Fix direction: either extend the same confidence field to proposed_note's construction path, or add an equivalent lighter-weight field there — the existing per-field confidence mechanism just needs to reach one more call site.

C. First-person-reflection → journal guidance isn't changing model behavior at all (id=14, high severity)

#75 added SKILL.md guidance for this exact scenario (a personal reflective journal entry discussing 1–2 external works in passing should resolve to the builtin journal type, "both/and" with resolving the referenced works). Confirmed present in the fb35e83 checkout — but 3 fresh test trials against the literal source produced zero behavioral change: still splits into two empty stub entities for the referenced works, still never attempts journal at all. This is now the 4th consecutive confirmation round with identical zero-variance failure on this exact source shape, across two different SKILL.md guidance attempts (round 2's #75 predecessor and this one). Worth escalating past prompt-guidance-only fixes — SKILL.md text isn't moving the needle here; may need either a stronger/more explicit trigger condition in the guidance (the current wording may not be getting weighted highly enough against competing signals) or a code-level heuristic (e.g. detect first-person voice + multiple dated sections + no single dominant external subject → route to journal) rather than relying on the model picking it up from prose guidance alone.

Once these are fixed and merged, I'll run another isolated-workspace confirmation pass the same way as the last four rounds. Same handoff format as WAKIL-FIXES-2026-07-27-round3.md when you're ready.

## Problem

This is the 4th consecutive confirmation round with zero-variance identical failure on the same source shape (a hand-authored, multi-date personal reflection discussing 1-2 external works in passing) — two separate `SKILL.md` guidance attempts (round 2's predecessor and #75/PR #83) have produced **no measurable behavioral change** across 3+ fresh test trials each: the source still splits into empty stub entities for the referenced works, `journal/` stays empty, every time.

Root cause, found this round: **#75's guidance was added to the wrong skill file.** `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`'s own docstring states its job precisely: "for each person, company, concept, project, or organization the source touched, does the knowledge base already have a page for it, should one be created, or should the mention be left alone?" — i.e. entity-resolution decides actions for entities the source *mentions*, never the type/shape of the source's own primary content. That decision — what `proposal.proposed_note` becomes — is made by the **first** model call (`_run_extraction`, `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`), using the source-type-specific skill (`article`/`text`/`transcript`). A hand-authored personal reflection is captured and ingested as `text`, so its `proposed_note` type is decided by `text/SKILL.md` — which has **zero** mention of recognizing a first-person reflection as a shape at all. Its own "judge the shape first" list is: "notes someone typed, a quoted exchange, a list, a draft" — no personal-reflection/journal option.

Since entity-resolution never controls or overrides `proposed_note`'s type for the source's own subject (only for *other* entities it mentions), #75's guidance was structurally incapable of ever affecting this outcome, regardless of wording — it was answering a question a different model call already had to have settled first. This fully explains the zero-variance failure across two independent guidance-wording attempts.

## Fix direction

Add "a first-person personal reflection about the day/period, even if it discusses external works in passing" as a recognized shape in `src/wakil/skills/text/SKILL.md`'s own "judge the shape first" guidance (and `article`/`transcript/SKILL.md` if either could plausibly ingest this shape too) — instructing that this shape should propose a `journal`-typed (or whichever dated-record type fits) `proposed_note` for its own content, the same "both/and, not either/or" framing #75 already established (correctly) for the entity-resolution side of this same coordination. Since `text/SKILL.md` is the skill actually deciding `proposed_note`'s type for this shape, this is the fix's correct location.

Given the history of two prior guidance attempts producing zero measurable effect (even though this round's specific defect was a location error, not necessarily a wording weakness), also seriously consider whether a **code-level backstop** is warranted this time: a deterministic heuristic (e.g. detecting multiple dated section headers combined with first-person pronoun density and no single dominant external-entity subject) that, when strongly indicated and `proposal.proposed_note` ends up null or non-journal-typed for such a source, either injects an explicit source-specific directive into the extraction prompt or corrects the outcome after the fact (mirroring `_correct_proposed_note_type`'s established "record the correction, never apply it invisibly" pattern from issue #73). Weigh this against the real risk of false positives forcing `journal` onto genuinely non-reflective sources — if you implement a heuristic, make it conservative and test it against a range of non-reflective source shapes (a book note, a meeting transcript, a reference article) to confirm it doesn't fire on them.
