### GitHub's release-page renderer mention-parses bare `@word` in the body, even when it doesn't name a real account

**Date:** 2026-07-28 · **Source:** the published `v0.1.0` GitHub Release page

The v0.1.0 release page showed a "Contributors" widget with two bogus avatars, labeled "file" and "url". The release body (generated by `git-cliff` from commit subjects) included the literal line `✨ feat(context): expand @file:/@url: references in context text` — describing wakil's own `@file:`/`@url:` context-reference syntax, not GitHub usernames. GitHub's release renderer scans the body for anything shaped like `@word` and treats every match as a user mention for the purposes of the "Contributors" widget (reflected in the release API's own `mentions_count` field), regardless of whether an account by that name exists or the surrounding text has nothing to do with attribution.

Fixed with a `git-cliff` `postprocessors` regex (`cliff.toml`) that wraps any `@word` in backticks before it reaches the rendered changelog/release notes — GitHub doesn't mention-parse inside code spans. The general lesson: any generated GitHub-rendered text (release notes, PR descriptions, issue bodies) that echoes source strings verbatim — commit subjects, code identifiers, doc text — can accidentally produce a real `@mention` if that source text ever contains an `@`-prefixed token, with no warning that it happened; check rendered output on the actual GitHub page, not just the raw markdown, when a changelog or generated body might contain code-like `@` syntax.

Already handled — that commit was the doc entry. Both issues are resolved and pushed:

**1. Contributors-avatar bug — fixed.** GitHub's release page mention-parses any bare `@word` in the body, and a commit describing wakil's own `@file:`/`@url:` context-reference syntax got misread as two user mentions. Fixed via a `git-cliff` postprocessor that wraps `@word` in backticks (code spans aren't mention-parsed), regenerated `CHANGELOG.md`, and retroactively edited the published `v0.1.0` release notes — the "Contributors" widget and its `mentions_count` are gone now. Documented in `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`.

**2. GitHub Packages — not a workflow bug, a real gap.** GitHub Packages doesn't support Python/PyPI-style packages at all — it supports npm, Maven/Gradle, RubyGems, NuGet, and Docker, but native Python package hosting has been a long-standing, still-open feature request ([github/roadmap#94](https://github.com/github/roadmap/issues/94)). There's no registry surface there to publish a wheel/sdist to, regardless of how the workflow is configured.

The release process was deliberately scoped to **GitHub Releases** (tagged, with wheel/sdist attached as downloadable assets) rather than a package registry — which is what's actually working on `v0.1.0`. If you want a real installable-registry experience, the options are:

options.description: Download the wheel/sdist from the Releases page, or pip/uv install directly from the git tag (e.g. uv tool install git+https://github.com/ebridges/wakil@v0.1.0). No registry, no extra publish step — already working.

options.label: Publish to PyPI
options.description: Real Python package index, installable via plain `pip install wakil`/`uv add wakil`. Requires making the repo public (or at least the package name), plus PyPI account/trusted-publisher setup. This was explicitly deferred out of scope when the release process was first designed, specifically because the repo was private.

options.label: Self-hosted/private index
options.description: e.g. a simple package index via GitHub Pages, or a private PyPI-compatible server. More infra to stand up and maintain for a single-user local-first tool -- likely overkill per CLAUDE.md's anti-over-engineering stance.

**Date:** 2026-07-28 · **Source:** the published `v0.1.0` GitHub Release page

The v0.1.0 release page showed a "Contributors" widget with two bogus avatars, labeled "file" and "url". The release body (generated by `git-cliff` from commit subjects) included the literal line `✨ feat(context): expand @file:/@url: references in context text` — describing wakil's own `@file:`/`@url:` context-reference syntax, not GitHub usernames. GitHub's release renderer scans the body for anything shaped like `@word` and treats every match as a user mention for the purposes of the "Contributors" widget (reflected in the release API's own `mentions_count` field), regardless of whether an account by that name exists or the surrounding text has nothing to do with attribution.

Fixed with a `git-cliff` `postprocessors` regex (`cliff.toml`) that wraps any `@word` in backticks before it reaches the rendered changelog/release notes — GitHub doesn't mention-parse inside code spans. The general lesson: any generated GitHub-rendered text (release notes, PR descriptions, issue bodies) that echoes source strings verbatim — commit subjects, code identifiers, doc text — can accidentally produce a real `@mention` if that source text ever contains an `@`-prefixed token, with no warning that it happened; check rendered output on the actual GitHub page, not just the raw markdown, when a changelog or generated body might contain code-like `@` syntax.

1	# Structured release process for wakil
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	`wakil` has never had a release: zero git tags, zero GitHub Releases, no PyPI presence. The only documented install path today is `git clone` + `uv sync` (README.md), and the version is hand-maintained as a static string in **two independent places** (`pyproject.toml`'s `version = "0.1.0"` and `src/wakil/__init__.py`'s `__version__ = "0.1.0"`) with nothing keeping them in sync. A `wakil version` CLI command already exists and reads `__init__.py`'s value, but that value is frozen and disconnected from anything real.
6	
7	The user now wants others to be able to install wakil, not just run it from a cloned checkout — which means version numbers, changelogs, and packaging need to hold up for an external consumer. At the same time, CLAUDE.md's explicit "avoid hosted product assumptions" / "local-first, single-user" framing is about wakil never becoming a multi-tenant *service* — it's not a prohibition on distributing wakil as an installable local CLI tool that individual people run on their own machines, which is what's being built here.
8	
9	Confirmed with the user: the repo stays **private** for now, so **PyPI publishing is out of scope for this pass** — distribution is via GitHub Releases (downloadable wheel/sdist attached to a tagged release, gated by repo access). Release cadence is **manual, periodic cut points** (not every merge), and the process should be **mostly automated** once the maintainer decides to cut one.
10	
11	## Decisions locked in
12	
13	1. **Versioning: git-tag-derived (`hatch-vcs`), not hand-maintained.** This removes the two-source-of-truth drift bug rather than adding complexity — one new build-system dependency, ~2 lines of config, and both existing version strings collapse into one (the git tag). First tag will be `v0.1.0` (matches current `pyproject.toml`, no artificial jump).
14	2. **Gating = re-run `ruff check` + `pytest -q` (includes the skill-lint suite already inside pytest) against the exact commit being tagged**, inside the release workflow itself — not by trusting a possibly-stale prior CI run.
15	3. **`ty` type-checking stays explicitly out of scope for this release process** (it's listed in CLAUDE.md's stated stack but was never wired in anywhere — standing it up is a separate, open-ended cleanup unrelated to release engineering). File a tracked GitHub issue for it as part of this work, so it's a deliberate deferral, not a silent drop.
16	4. **Changelog via `git-cliff`, user-facing commit types only** (`feat`/`fix`/`perf`/`refactor`/`docs`) — `chore`/`build`/`ci`/`test`/`style`/merge commits are grouped but excluded from the generated changelog body, keeping release notes readable.
17	5. **No PyPI step in this pass.** Distribution is GitHub Releases with wheel + sdist attached. The workflow is structured so adding a PyPI-publish step later (once repo-visibility is decided) is a small, additive change, not a redesign.
18	
19	## Implementation
20	
21	### 1. Versioning (`pyproject.toml`, `src/wakil/__init__.py`)
22	
23	`pyproject.toml`:
24	- Remove `version = "0.1.0"` from `[project]`, add `dynamic = ["version"]`.
25	- `[build-system] requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]`.
26	- Add `[tool.hatch.version]\nsource = "vcs"`.
27	
28	`src/wakil/__init__.py`: replace the hardcoded `__version__ = "0.1.0"` with a runtime lookup:
29	```python
30	from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version
31	
32	try:
33	    __version__ = version("wakil")
34	except PackageNotFoundError:
35	    __version__ = "0.0.0+unknown"
36	```
37	No change needed to `src/wakil/cli/main.py` — the existing `wakil version` command (line ~1559) already prints `wakil.__version__`; it will just start reporting a real value.
38	
39	Note: `hatch-vcs` needs git tags present to compute a version, so any CI/release workflow checkout must use `fetch-depth: 0`.
40	
41	### 2. Changelog generation (`cliff.toml`, new)
42	
43	New file at repo root, configured to:
44	- Parse the project's actual commit convention (gitmoji prefix + Conventional Commits type, e.g. `✨ feat(ingest): ...`) via `commit_parsers` regexes tolerant of the leading emoji — `conventional_commits = false`, custom parsers per type.
45	- Group `feat`→"✨ Features", `fix`→"🐛 Bug Fixes", `perf`→"⚡ Performance", `refactor`→"♻️ Refactoring", `docs`→"📝 Documentation".
46	- `skip = true` on `chore`/`build`/`ci`/`test`/`style` groups and on `Merge pull request` commits, so they're parsed but not shown.
47	- `tag_pattern = "v[0-9]*"`.
48	
49	`CHANGELOG.md` doesn't exist yet — the first release run creates it.
50	
51	### 3. Release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, new)
52	
53	Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` only —
54	```yaml
55	inputs:
56	  bump: {type: choice, options: [patch, minor, major], default: patch, required: true}
57	  dry_run: {type: boolean, default: false}
58	```
59	The maintainer picks the bump type explicitly (not auto-detected from commits) — keeps "what kind of release this is" a human call.
60	
61	Permissions: `contents: write` only (no `id-token`/OIDC needed without a PyPI step).
62	
63	Steps:
64	1. `actions/checkout@v7` with `fetch-depth: 0`.
65	2. `astral-sh/setup-uv@v8.3.2`, `uv sync --locked`.
66	3. Gate: `uv run ruff check .`.
67	4. Gate: `uv run pytest -q`.
68	5. Compute next version from the latest `v*` tag (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v*'`, default `v0.0.0` if none) + `inputs.bump`; export `NEW_VERSION`/`NEW_TAG`.
69	6. `uvx git-cliff --tag "$NEW_TAG" -o CHANGELOG.md` (full file) and `uvx git-cliff --tag "$NEW_TAG" --unreleased --strip all` (captured to a scratch `release-notes.md` for the Release body — not committed).
70	7. If not `dry_run`: commit `CHANGELOG.md` (`📝 docs(changelog): $NEW_TAG`), then create+push the annotated tag `$NEW_TAG` on that commit (tag must come after the changelog commit so `hatch-vcs` reads the right ref).
71	8. `uv build` — run *after* tagging so `hatch-vcs` picks up the new tag; produces `dist/*.whl` + `dist/*.tar.gz`.
72	9. Sanity check: confirm the built wheel filename's version matches `NEW_VERSION` — fail loudly on mismatch rather than publish something wrong.
73	10. If `dry_run`: upload `dist/*` + `release-notes.md` as workflow artifacts, stop (no push/tag/release).
74	11. If not `dry_run`: `gh release create "$NEW_TAG" dist/* --title "$NEW_TAG" --notes-file release-notes.md`.
75	
76	### 4. `ty` gap — file a tracked issue
77	
78	File a GitHub issue on `ebridges/wakil` (e.g. "Wire up `ty` type-checking as a CI gate") documenting: CLAUDE.md's stack lists `ty`, it has never been configured or run against the codebase, and standing it up (config + baseline triage of whatever it flags + adding it to `ci.yml`) is separate, open-ended work relative to this release process.
79	
80	### 5. README install section
81	
82	Add a short "Install a release" section to `README.md` alongside the existing `git clone` + `uv sync` dev-setup instructions, documenting how to install from a tagged GitHub Release once one exists (e.g. downloading the wheel asset from the Releases page and `pip install`/`uv tool install`-ing it, or `uv tool install git+https://github.com/ebridges/wakil@vX.Y.Z`).
83	
84	## Verification
85	
86	- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pytest -q` stay green throughout (no regressions from the `__init__.py`/`pyproject.toml` changes).
87	- Locally: `uv build` after the `pyproject.toml`/`__init__.py` changes and confirm the built wheel's version is derived correctly from a test tag (`git tag v0.1.0-test && uv build`, inspect `dist/*.whl` filename, then delete the test tag).
88	- `wakil version` (or `uv run wakil version`) prints the real, tag-derived version, not a frozen string.
89	- Trigger `release.yml` once via `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run: true` first to confirm the whole pipeline (gates → version compute → changelog → build → version-match check) works end to end without pushing anything, before ever running it for real.
90	- First real run: `workflow_dispatch` with `bump: patch, dry_run: false` → confirm `v0.1.0` tag, `CHANGELOG.md` commit, and GitHub Release with attached `dist/` artifacts all appear as expected.
91
